assertions.assertion: Data extraction correctly identifies CVE-2026-31812, library quinn-proto, affected range < 0.11.14, and fixed version 0.11.14 from the Vulnerability issue (Step 1)
assertions.evidence: data-extraction.md Step 1 table: CVE ID = CVE-2026-31812, Vulnerable library = quinn-proto, Affected version range = < 0.11.14, Fixed version = 0.11.14

assertions.assertion: Data extraction identifies the ecosystem as Cargo based on the library name and component context (Step 1 Ecosystem detection)
assertions.evidence: data-extraction.md Ecosystem Detection section: 'Library name: quinn-proto -- a Rust crate (identified by the crate naming convention and Cargo ecosystem context from the Ecosystem Mappings table)' and 'Ecosystem: Cargo'

assertions.assertion: Version impact table includes ALL versions from the security-matrix.md supportability matrix — no versions are skipped (Important Rule 4)
assertions.evidence: version-impact.md Section 2.4 includes all 7 versions: 2.1.0, 2.1.1 (2.1.x stream) and 2.2.0, 2.2.1, 2.2.2, 2.2.3, 2.2.4 (2.2.x stream). Section 2.1 confirms 'Both streams (2.1.x and 2.2.x) are included per Important Rule 4: Check ALL supported versions.'

assertions.assertion: Version impact analysis uses pinned commit tags from the supportability matrix for each version, not branch HEAD (Important Rule 13)
assertions.evidence: version-impact.md Section 2.3: 'All dependency versions extracted using pinned commit tags from the supportability matrix (Important Rule 13). Released versions use the exact commit from the matrix, never HEAD or any branch tip.' Table shows specific tags: v0.3.8, v0.3.12, v0.4.5, v0.4.8, v0.4.11, v0.4.12 with 'git show <tag>:Cargo.lock' sources.

assertions.assertion: Version impact table identifies retag versions and carries forward the affected status from the original version (Important Rule 5)
assertions.evidence: version-impact.md: 'Version 2.2.2 is identified as a retag of 2.2.1 (both use backend tag v0.4.8). The lock file check was skipped for 2.2.2 and the affected status was carried forward from 2.2.1: quinn-proto 0.11.12, YES (affected).'

assertions.assertion: Affects Versions correction proposes replacing PSIRT-assigned versions with lock-file-verified versions, showing the diff (Step 3.2)
assertions.evidence: affects-versions.md Section 3.2 Proposed Correction shows: 'Current: [RHTPA 2.0.0] / Proposed: [RHTPA 2.2.0, RHTPA 2.2.1, RHTPA 2.2.2]' with rationale explaining RHTPA 2.0.0 does not exist in the supportability matrix.

assertions.assertion: Affects Versions correction references version names from the supportability matrix rather than hardcoded Jira version IDs (Important Rule 6)
assertions.evidence: affects-versions.md: Uses version names RHTPA 2.2.0, RHTPA 2.2.1, RHTPA 2.2.2 throughout, and explicitly states 'Version IDs are discovered dynamically at runtime (Important Rule 6) -- no hardcoded Jira version IDs are used.' The proposed mutation uses placeholder IDs like '<RHTPA-2.2.0-jira-id>'.

assertions.assertion: Remediation tasks include Repository, Target Branch, acceptance criteria, and dependency linkage between upstream and downstream tasks (Important Rule 9)
assertions.evidence: remediation.md Task 1 includes Repository (rhtpa-backend), Target Branch (release/0.4.z), Acceptance Criteria (3 items), and Dependencies (Depends on TC-8001). Task 2 includes Repository (rhtpa-release.0.4.z), Target Branch (main), Acceptance Criteria, and Dependencies with Blocks link (upstream -> downstream).

assertions.assertion: For Cargo ecosystem, remediation creates two tasks: upstream backport task and downstream propagation subtask with Blocks dependency (Important Rule 8)
assertions.evidence: remediation.md creates Task 1 (Upstream Backport Task) and Task 2 (Downstream Propagation Subtask). Linkage summary table shows 'Blocks | <upstream-task-key> | <downstream-task-key> | Downstream blocked until upstream merges'.

assertions.assertion: The analysis presents triage recommendations as proposed actions — framing Affects Versions changes, label additions, and status transitions as proposals rather than executed mutations (Guardrails)
assertions.evidence: affects-versions.md uses 'Proposed Correction', 'Proposed Jira Mutation (requires engineer confirmation)'. remediation.md uses 'Proposed Jira creation:' and concludes with 'All proposed Jira mutations require explicit engineer confirmation before execution.' data-extraction.md Step 0.7 uses 'Proposed action:' throughout.

assertions.assertion: The data-extraction output describes Step 0.7 actions before the Step 1 data table: assigning the CVE issue to the current user and transitioning it to Assigned status (Step 0.7)
assertions.evidence: data-extraction.md begins with '# Step 0.7 -- Early Assignment and Status Transition' before '# Step 1 -- Data Extraction'. Step 0.7 describes: (1) retrieving current user's Jira account ID, (2) assigning TC-8001 to the current user, (3) discovering available transitions, and (4) transitioning to Assigned status.
